OpenStax, Psychology, ch. 6 summary — instincts and reflexes as innate, and the three basic forms of learning

visual.title: Naming the four parts, and the shape of the curve
visual.alt: The four conditioning labels laid out before, during and after training, with food as the unconditioned stimulus producing salivation as the unconditioned response, the bell presented about half a second before the food, and the bell afterwards producing a usually weaker conditioned response; a curve of conditioned-response strength rising through acquisition, falling through extinction, and reappearing by itself after a rest; a generalisation gradient falling away from the trained stimulus; and a panel on taste aversion as the exception, with the amygdala for fear conditioning and the cerebellum for eyeblink conditioning.
visual.caption: Label the unconditioned pair first — the thing that works without training and the reflex it produces — and the conditioned pair is whatever is left. Spontaneous recovery after a rest is the evidence that extinction never deleted the original association.
